Appearances:
Sh. Rekha Sharma, Advocate for appellant.
Sh. Manoj Kr. Garg, Ld. Chief Pp for State/FSAT.
Judgment:

1. This Judgment shall decide the instant appeal filed by the appellants under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as amended upto date (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing ex part order dated 25.02.2022 passed by Sh. D. Karthikeyan, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Addl.

1

Magistrate, New Delhi District (for short Ld. AO/ADM), whereby the appellants have been convicted for being found in violation of Section 23(1), 26(1), 26(2) (ii) & 27(1) read with Section 3(1)(zf) of the FSS Act and also for violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4,
2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging &
Labeling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter referred as 'FSS (P&L) Regulation'), thereby making them punishable under Section 52 of the FSS Act.

FACTUAL MATRIX:
2. In a nutshell, appellant No.4 is a company and running a Restaurant having its registered office at G72, First Floor, Connaught Place, New Delhi110001
and the appellant No.1 Sh. Ravi Tickoo is the FBOcum Chef while appellant Nos. 2 and 3 are the Directors of appellant No.4.

It is stated that on 12.09.2019 at about 6.30 p.m.
Smt. Anjali Bhardwaj, Food Safety Officer alongwith the then FSO Sh. Pankaj Kumar Meena visited the premises of M/s. Lord of Drinks for random inspection and appellant No.1 readily cooperated with them providing them access to the premises including the Kitchen and dining area and the FSO purchased four portions of 'Kabuli Chana' for analysis, which were ready for use in preparation of 'hummus (Lebanese dish) and no price was paid since the sample was not for direct sale.

It is stated that on 08.04.2021 a complaint was filed by FSO, namely Sh. Kuldeep Singh Suman against the appellants as per Rule 3.1.1.(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules,
2011 but no notice or summons was issued to the appellants and without opportunity of hearing the impugned order dated 25.02.2022 was passed imposing not only consolidated penalty upon the appellants but also Mr. Satya Narayan Sharma, who was found to be Proprietor and Packer of the food item.

The impugned order is assailed by the appellant Nos. 1 to 4 inter alia on the grounds that the Ld. AO/ADM failed to consider that the appellants were not manufacturer of the product and the 'kabuli chana' was not meant for direct sale and was for ultimate consumption; and that the Ld. AO/ADM passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner overlooking the fact that FSO while collecting the sample on 12.09.2019 filledup form VA wherein all the details of the food item including label declaration such as batch number, net weight, expiry date, date of packing/manufacturing, license number, and best before period were clearly spelled out and yet the Ld. AO/ADM held that food item was 'misbranded'.
3.

It is pertinent to mention here that the FSO in the complaint dated 08.04.2021 stated that on lifting the samples of the food item viz.
Kabuli chana for analysis price of the same amounting to Rs. 1400/ was offered but it was not accepted and four sealed packets each weighing 2 kg of food item viz. Kabuli chana were taken as samples and the same was sent to Food Analyst, Government of Delhi for analysis, who vide report No. FSS/ 1377/2019 dated 20.09.2019 opined that sample was 'misbranded' because there were galore violations with regard to Regulation No. 2.2.1.5, 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7,
2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 and 2.2.2.10.

PROCEEDINGS IN THE APPEAL:
Sh. Ravi Tickoo S/O Sh. S.K. Tickoo vs Food Safety Officer on 28 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77675082/
2 4.

On filing of the present appeal on 02.09.2022 the operation of the impugned order was stayed subject to the appellants depositing/furnishing Demand Draft/FDR in the sum of Rs. 50% of the fine/penalty imposed by the Ld. AO/ADM and the said order has been complied with.
Notice was issued to the respondent and although no reply is filed, the appeal is opposed and the record of the Ld. AO/ADM is produced.

DECISION:
5. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the parties at the Bar.
I have also perused the record of the present appeal as also the original record of the Ld. AO/ADM.
At the outset, the impugned order dated 25.02.2022 cannot be sustained in law.

Section 3(1) (zf) defines that 'misbranded food' means an article of food, which is purported or represented to be being used and offered or promoted for sale with false, misleading or deceptive claims either upon the lable of the packet or through advertisement.

It would be suffice to state that regulation 2.2.1.5 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation provides that the contents of the label shall be clear, prominent, indelible and readily legible by the consumer under normal conditions of purchase and use.
Regulation 2.2.1.7 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation provides that license number shall be displayed on the principal display panel.
Regulation 2.2.2.1 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation provides that name of food shall include trade name or description of food contained in the package.
Regulation 2.2.2.4 then provides for declaration as to the item being 'veg' or 'non veg' by a particular symbol.
Further, 2.2.2.6 stipulates requirement of name and complete address of the manufacturer and the net quantity is to be declared vide regulation 2.2.2.7.

Further, lot/code/batch identification is stipulated to be identical and best before date by virtue of regulations 2.2.2.9 and 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L)
Regulation respectively.

6. That being the legal proposition, the Food Analyst report dated 20.09.2019, as regards the label on the food items, whereby it was reported or opined that it was without declaration of 'veg' symbol and without expiry date in place of best before declaration and the other declaration like, name of food, net weight, packaging date,
batch number and FSSAI License number were 'illegible', is not fathomable.

It is not explained as to how while conducting the proceedings at the spot by the FSO, form VA clearly described the food item, net weight, batch number and packing date,
expiry date as also FSSAI license number.
The scanned copy of the form VA is annexed with this Judgment as 'Annexure A'.
If the said aspects were perceived by the FSO, it is not palatable as to how Food Analyst in his report dated 20.09.2019 held that declaration on the label were 'illegible'.
It goes without saying that the food item in question was not found to be adulterated or substandard in any manner.
Except for a minor nondeclration on the item being 'veg', other regulations were being duly complied with.

Sh. Ravi Tickoo S/O Sh. S.K. Tickoo vs Food Safety Officer on 28 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77675082/
3 7.

sentences.text: All said and done, the impugned order was passed without issuing any notice upon the appellants.

A bare perusal of the record of the Ld. AO/ADM would show that there was no proof of delivery with regard to service of notice upon appellant Nos.1 to 4 and only respondent No.5 appeared in person and conceded his mistake.

The impugned order by the Ld. AO/ADM was also in derogation to the Advisory issued by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for being nonactionable minor infringement and the Ld. AO/ADM overlooked the provisions of Section 80 (B) (2)
(D) of the FSS Act and there was no cause of action against the present appellants so as to visit them with such an exorbitant penalty by virtue of impugned order.

sentences.text: 8. In view of the foregoing discussions, the present appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 25.02.2022 qua the appellants is setaside.
The demand draft/FDR placed by the appellants on the record in terms of directions of this Court be returned to the appellants forthwith as per rules.
The Record of the Ld. AO/ADM be returned along with the copy of the Judgment.
File of appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
